generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Sample from the parent table's generated primary-key values; include at least one parent row with no children and, where nullable, at least one NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.int_numeric: Uniform integer within the column's range rule; include boundary values and one step on each side of any listed literal.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real within the column's range rule; include boundary values and one step on each side of any listed literal.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from the column's value pool or enum; include near-variants (case changes, trailing spaces) of listed equality literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Short readable strings; allow near-duplicate values when no constraint forbids it.
generic_sampling_rules.text_day_of_week: One of Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database's observed share (0.0 in the shown statistics, so keep NULLs rare but present).

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: all shown rows have low <= high

generation_specification.uncertainty: The shown sample has fewer rows than the statistics (e.g. station 8 vs 11, train 8 vs 11, route 8 vs 18, weekly_weather 8 vs 16); generation sizes are kept below original sizes. NULL shares are observed as 0.0 but nullable columns still receive at least one NULL per instruction 10. The aggregate_boundary target on weekly_weather.day_of_week (MAX > 50) is nonsensical for a text day column and is treated as a sampling-domain note only.

issues.evidence: The spec's per_column_exceptions entry for weekly_weather.day_of_week lists pattern 'aggregate_boundary' with targets aggregate MAX(weekly_weather.day_of_week) > 50 and values [49,50,51]. day_of_week is a text column constrained to Monday..Sunday (semantic rule day_of_week IN (...)). The spec's own uncertainty note admits this 'is nonsensical for a text day column and is treated as a sampling-domain note only'. No semantic rule or formula supports a MAX(day_of_week) > 50 predicate.
issues.requested_revision: Drop or re-classify the weekly_weather.day_of_week aggregate_boundary exception to an explicit 'ignored / unsupported' note so the specification does not carry an unevidenced constraint. This is a documentation cleanup only and does not affect generated instances (the program already treats it as a domain note and generates the 7-day enum).

issues.evidence: The spec records per-column group-size targets '1, 2 and >= 3' on train.id, train.name, station.id, station.network_name, station.local_authority, weekly_weather.station_id, route.station_id. Only route.train_id / route.station_id / weekly_weather.station_id are FK-group columns where the pattern is naturally realised; for train.id, station.id and the text columns the 'group_sizes' targets refer to grouping parent rows with children, which the program achieves only indirectly (via fresh PKs plus FK group assignment), and no semantic rule pins sizes 1/2/>=3 on those text columns themselves.
issues.requested_revision: Either clarify that the group-size targets on parent rows are met through the child-side FK assignment (route.train_id, route.station_id, weekly_weather.station_id), or drop the exceptions on train.id / station.id / text columns. Execution shows no integrity failures, so this is a specification clarity issue rather than a blocking error.

issues.evidence: The semantic rule weekly_weather.low_temperature <= high_temperature is implemented in instance.py: after sampling, low > high is corrected by setting lo[i] = hi[i] - rng.randint(0,5). This 'repairs' the value rather than only constraining sampling. It is consistent with the three-valued-logic rule (only non-NULL operands constrained), so it is not a blocker, but it can slightly shift the low_temperature distribution away from the sampled range and its boundary values.
issues.requested_revision: Prefer generating low_temperature within [domain.lo, high_temperature] at draw time (e.g., a dependent sampler bound by the already-chosen high value) so the range/boundary planting of low_temperature is preserved. Document either approach; no blocking change required.

issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback: all 13 nullable columns report 'NULL ... / n' (e.g., station.network_name NULL 20/162, train.interval NULL 20/161, weekly_weather.wind_speed_mph NULL 19/186), satisfying the NULL rule (>=1 NULL per instance plus non-NULL rows). NOT NULL / PK columns show no NULL-vs-rule failures. weekly_weather.low_temperature NULL 14/186 vs high_temperature NULL 16/186 are independent, and rows where one side is NULL are not constrained (three-valued logic), which matches the rule.
issues.requested_revision: None; noted as compliant. The compact share is ~0.0, and the program plants >=1 NULL per nullable column per instance, so 'rare but present' is met.

unresolved_checks: Spec boundary planting for weekly_weather.precipitation lists values [-38,-37,-36,49,50,51], including negatives that violate the semantic rule precipitation >= 0. NumberSampler.numeric() clamps values below domain.lo (0) to 0, so the negative boundary literals -38/-37/-36 will never be planted; only the positive side (49/50/51 around the >50 predicate) can appear. This is a designer/spec tension (compare vs aggregate boundary literals straddle 0 and >50), resolved silently by clamping; it does not break the precipitation >= 0 rule but means the negative literals are unexercised. Recommend the designer reconcile the boundary list with the >= 0 rule.
